question: Why is charge on a body always written as $q = ne$? Justify why $n$ cannot be a fraction.

options.A: $q=ne$ because charge can take any real value; $n$ may be fractional
options.B: $q=ne$ because the electron charge varies from body to body; $n$ must be a prime number
options.C: $q=ne$ because all charges are positive; $n$ is always zero
options.D: $q=ne$ because charge is gained or lost in whole electrons; $n$ is an integer and cannot be fractional
